evidence: backend/servers/reality-server/src/routes/users.rs:150-176 (pub async fn register, POST /api/v1/users/register) — on an email that is already registered the handler returns a distinct HTTP 409 CONFLICT with body "An account with this email already exists", whereas a fresh email returns HTTP 200 "Registration successful. Please check your email to verify your account.". The status + body differ by account existence, so an unauthenticated attacker can enumerate which emails have portal accounts by POSTing candidate emails and observing 409 vs 200. This is a PUBLIC, unauthenticated endpoint (users.rs:45-47 mount it alongside login, already flagged for no-rate-limit) so enumeration is cheap and unthrottled.

INCONSISTENCY with this same file's deliberate anti-enumeration posture: request_password_reset (users.rs:405-458) is explicitly documented "the response is intentionally identical regardless of whether the email exists, to avoid letting attackers enumerate accounts" and returns a uniform 200. The register path leaks the exact signal that password-reset was hardened to hide, so an attacker simply uses /register instead of /password-reset to enumerate. The already-tracked finding code-review-reality-server-login-sso-account-enum (2026-07-16, handlers/users/mod.rs:251, the LOGIN path) is a DIFFERENT endpoint — no prior signal or backlog row covers the register endpoint. Verified net-new against all 61 reality-server signal files and backlog ids.

Impact: account/email enumeration (OWASP WSTG-IDNT-04) — privacy leak + reconnaissance for credential-stuffing/phishing against confirmed portal users. Severity medium (info-disclosure, not a direct bypass); registration enumeration is a frequently-accepted tradeoff, but here the codebase's own password-reset flow establishes the enumeration-safe contract, and register already issues an email-verification step so it can adopt the same pattern cleanly.

Suggested fix (implementer): make register enumeration-safe to match password-reset — always return the same 200 "check your email" envelope regardless of whether the email is new or already registered; when the email already exists, send an "account already exists / sign in or reset password" email instead of a verification email (so a real owner is still informed out-of-band), and never surface the 409 existence signal to the HTTP caller. Alternatively, if product requires the inline "email taken" UX, gate the register endpoint behind the same rate limiter + CAPTCHA and document the accepted-enumeration decision. Regenerate the OpenAPI/clients if the 409 response is removed from the contract.
